title: Five sheets compose Tooltip and none of them imports its stylesheet
foundBy: consumer report on three applications pinned to 0.2.1-dev, verified against 0c015ef

evidence.verified: Six sheets now import what their component renders: `card.css`, `table.css`, `tree.css`, `theme-toggle.css` and `event-lanes.css` take `tooltip.css`, and `event-lanes.css` also takes `chart-tooltip.css`. The sixth was found by the check written for this, not by the report. Removing the import from `card.css` fails `check-integrity` with `Card renders Tooltip but this sheet does not @import "./tooltip.css"`, and the restore is byte-identical. `npm run ci` exits 0 at f11b338.

details:
A component sheet in this package imports the sheets of what it renders. `table.css` imports `button.css`, `dropdown.css`, `search-input.css` and `skeleton.css`; `tree.css` imports three; `sectioned-tree.css` imports three; `card.css` imports `skeleton.css`.

None of the five sheets whose component renders a `Tooltip` imports `tooltip.css`. Those are `card.css`, `table.css`, `tree.css`, `theme-toggle.css` and `event-lanes.css`, and the last two import nothing at all.

A consumer loading per-component sheets therefore has a working page until a tooltip opens. Without the sheet the bubble has no `position: fixed`, so it lays out in flow at the end of the body and moves the page under the pointer. `ThemeToggle` wraps its control in a `Tooltip` unconditionally, so one click on the theme toggle is enough.

Three applications reported this. All three load per-component sheets, none imports `tooltip.css`, and none renders a `Tooltip` directly. The convention is already right everywhere else, which is why nobody noticed the one place it was not applied.

notes.text:
A check now holds the import graph against the component sources, so this cannot drift again. It is in `check-integrity.mjs` as `sheet-imports`, and it earned its place before it was committed: it reported that `EventLanes` renders a `ChartTooltip` while `event-lanes.css` imported no `chart-tooltip.css`. All three reporting applications render `EventLanes`, so that instance was live for them and nobody had found it.

The consumer's own suggestion, a `requires` field in the spec frontmatter, was not needed. The `@import` graph is already that declaration and is machine readable, so what was missing was something holding it to the source rather than a second copy of it to keep in step.
